question: What walking speed is generally used to calculate pedestrian clearance time, and what alternative speed may be used with an extended push-button feature?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The pedestrian clearance time is generally calculated using a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second, measured from the curb or edge of pavement to the far side of the traveled way or a sufficient median. Where an extended push button press function is installed to let slower pedestrians request more crossing time, a walking speed of up to 4 feet per second may be used instead. Additionally, the combined walk interval and clearance time should accommodate a slower 3 feet per second speed measured from the pedestrian detector, and slower speeds should be considered where slower pedestrians or wheelchair users routinely cross. Guidance (recommended): - Except as provided in Paragraph 8, the pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian who left the curb or edge of pavement at the end of the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication "to travel at a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second to at least the far side of the traveled way or to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait." - Where pedestrians who walk slower than 3.5 feet per second, or pedestrians who use wheelchairs, routinely use the crosswalk, a walking speed of less than 3.5 feet per second should be considered in determining the pedestrian clearance time. - The total of the walk interval and pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian who left the pedestrian detector (or, if no detector is present, a location 6 feet behind the face of the curb or edge of pavement) at the beginning of the WALKING PERSON indication to travel at a walking speed of 3 feet per second to the far side of the traveled way (or median for a two-stage crossing); any additional time required should be added to the walk interval. Options (permitted): - "A walking speed of up to 4 feet per second may be used to evaluate the sufficiency of the pedestrian clearance time at locations where an extended push button press function has been installed to provide slower pedestrians an opportunity to request and receive a longer pedestrian clearance time." Passive pedestrian detection may also be used to automatically adjust the clearance time based on the pedestrian's actual walking speed or actual clearance of the crosswalk. - The additional time provided by an extended push button press to satisfy pedestrian clearance time needs may be added to either the walk interval or the pedestrian change interval. - Pedestrians may be provided with additional features such as increased crossing time, audible beaconing, or a speech push button information message as a result of an extended push button press. Citations: - Section 4I.06 Guidance §7 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Option §8 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Option §9 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §10 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §14 (p.725) - Section 4K.05 Option §1 (p.734)
gold_answer: The general walking speed is 3.5 feet per second. Up to 4 feet per second may be used to evaluate sufficiency where an extended push-button press provides slower pedestrians a longer clearance time.
